highlights.text: “There is an entire world, Shallan,” Jasnah said, “of which our minds skim but the surface. A world of deep, profound thought. A world created by deep, profound thoughts. When you see Shadesmar, you enter those depths. It is an alien place to us in some ways, but at the same time we formed it. With some help.”

“By my best guess, spren are elements of the Cognitive Realm that have leaked into the physical world. They’re concepts that have gained a fragment of sentience, perhaps because of human intervention.
It was a brutal truth. The best truths, however, were simple.
“I know . . . little of humans,” Pattern said. “They break. Their minds break. You did not break. Only cracked.”
There was no fighting against what she had become. The eyes of the gods were too strongly upon her.
“We did need new tactics,” Thude said. “But this . . . Something’s wrong with you, Eshonai.”
Some people—like a festering finger or a leg shattered beyond repair—just needed to be removed.

“It is an era for tyrants. I doubt this place is ready for anything more, and a benevolent tyrant is preferable to the disaster of weak rule. Perhaps in another place and time, I’d have denounced you with spit and bile. Here, today, I praise you as what this world needs.”
“I’d pay to see that.” “Me skipping?” “You happy,”
